sections.title: Recognition and core idea
sections.markdown:
## When to recognize this pattern
Look for key-to-value lookup through a hash function, repeated work, or a prompt whose constraints rule out a quadratic scan.

## Core idea
A hash map (Python dictionary) applies a hash function to a key and resolves collisions internally. Lookup, insertion, and deletion are O(1) average, not guaranteed worst-case. It excels at counting, grouping, and remembering previously seen values.

sections.title: From naive to better
sections.learning_objective: Derive the optimized approach from a baseline.
sections.markdown:
## Naive approach
Start with nested-loop search. It may be easy to verify, but it repeats work and becomes too slow as input grows. State its cost before optimizing.

## Better approach
Use counting and complement lookup. The optimization is valid only if the invariant proves discarded work cannot affect the answer. Never quote a complexity without identifying the operation that dominates it.

sections.title: Complexity and common mistakes
sections.markdown:
## Time complexity
O(n) average time. Explain whether sorting or preprocessing is included.

## Space complexity
O(n) keys and values. Input storage does not count as auxiliary space unless copied.

## Common mistakes
Using the pattern without its precondition, moving state in the wrong order, missing empty input, mishandling duplicates, and reporting average-case cost as a guarantee. For recursion, include call-stack space; for a DP table or hash map, count stored states.

sections.title: Arena transfer practice
sections.learning_objective: Transfer the pattern without copying a solution.
sections.markdown:
## Arena reference
Practice with `dsa-two-sum-indices` in Forge Arena. First restate the invariant and complexity target, then implement from a blank editor. If stuck, use progressive hints only after writing the naive approach. After submission, test one normal case, one boundary case, and one adversarial case. Arena correctness is deterministic; an explanation is useful only when it matches the code's behavior.
key_points: Independent recall is stronger evidence than assisted completion.
